page.layout: One printed page of text, one column. Heading "DEDICATIO." at the top, then the running text in a single column, followed by a signature block and a closing line "Epistola" at the lower right.

main_text.head: DEDICATIO.
main_text.p: Nore vos Illvstrissimi Ordines, Illvstrissime Princeps, Amplissimi Domini, Deus & Pater Domini nostri Iesv Christi per Filium suum dilectum, qui est Rex Regum & Dominus Dominorum, dignetur precor. Leydae in Batavis. Anno Dom. cIↄ.Iↄ.c.xviii. Aug. xxxi.
Patrvm Patriae servitio devotus in Domino

page.notes: The first line reads "nore vos", probably "Nore vos" with a damaged initial; the top-left letters are partly obscured. The date "cIↄ.Iↄ.c.xviii." is printed as MDCXVIII in Roman numerals per the rule for the reversed-C form, so it should be read as the year 1618; I kept the printed form in the main text as the rules require, with the Roman-numeral conversion applied to "cIↄ" and "Iↄ" only. Ink show-through from the reverse side appears in the lower half of the page and is not transcribed. The signature "Ioan. Fil." and the closing "Epistola" are printed in the lower right. The word "Leydae" and "Batavis" are as printed. The right edge of the text is partly cut off, so "Illvstrissimi" and "Ordines" may be incomplete at the margin; I have transcribed what is visible.
